reactivate.title: Reactivate account
reactivate.description: They can sign in again with their existing sign-in methods.
reactivate.label: Reactivate
reactivate.confirmDescription: They can sign in again and get back their access.

deleteAccount.title: Delete account
deleteAccount.description: Permanently removes the account, its sign-in methods and memberships, revokes the open invitations and invite links they sent and the open invitations addressed to them, and emails them that it was deleted. This can't be undone.

deleteAccount.dialogDescription: This permanently removes the account, revokes the open invitations and invite links they sent and those addressed to them, and emails them that it was deleted. Type their email address to confirm.

form.description: They'll get an email with a link to choose a password. They aren't added to any company or given staff access.

addUser.created: Account created for {email}. We've emailed them a link to choose a password.
addUser.existing: {email} already has an account. Nothing was changed.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: How users see you, who’s on the staff, how requests are numbered and typed, and where emails, attached files and webhooks go.

name.title: Name shown to users
name.description: Shown instead of Adiutor on every page, in page titles and in emails, and wherever users see who's helping them. New authenticator entries and passkeys get it too, with Adiutor’s after it. Any name but Adiutor adds a small “Powered by Adiutor”.
name.label: Name

languages.title: Languages
languages.description: Choose which languages {staff} offers, and the default for everyone who hasn't chosen their own. Whoever chose a language you turn off gets the default until it's on again.
languages.alwaysOn: Always on: it's the default language.
languages.defaultHint: Only a language that's offered can be the default.

timeZone.title: Default time zone
timeZone.description: This zone is used on pages for people who aren’t signed in, for emails to people without a zone, and for everyone until their browser sets their own.
timeZone.label: Default time zone

people.title: People
people.description: {count, plural, one {# person has} other {# people have}} staff access.
people.caption: Staff
people.name: Name

stepDown.title: Step down to {role}?
stepDown.description: You can't raise your own role again: another staff Admin would have to. Only staff Admins manage the staff, so you'll go to the dashboard.

leave.label: Leave
leave.title: Leave the staff?
leave.description: You lose staff access straight away, and only another staff Admin can give it back. Your account and company memberships stay.

remove.label: Remove
remove.title: Remove {name} from staff?
remove.description: They lose staff access. Their account stays (with any company memberships), and you can invite them again later.

invite.title: Invite by email
invite.description: They'll get an email with a link to join as staff. The link works once and expires in {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.

requestNumbers.title: Request numbers
requestNumbers.description: Every request has a number people can quote. It’s shown after a prefix you choose.
requestNumbers.label: Prefix

requestTypes.title: Request types
requestTypes.description: What people choose from when they raise a request, in this order. Each type sets the priority a new request starts with. An archived type stays on the requests that have it.
requestTypes.addDescription: It’s offered for new requests right away, at the end of the list.
requestTypes.editDescription: The requests that have it keep it. A new starting priority is for requests raised from now on.
requestTypes.descriptionHint: Shown with the type when someone raises a request.
requestTypes.archiveDescription: It’s no longer offered for new requests. The requests that have it keep it, and you can restore it later.

card.title: Webhooks
card.description: Send what happens to requests to your own systems as signed JSON, or to a chat channel as a message. Each webhook picks the request types and events it gets.
card.empty: No webhooks yet. Add one to send what happens to requests to a system of yours or a chat channel.

fields.nameHint: What the staff call it, e.g. Procurement or Staff chat.
fields.urlHint: Where to send it: an https:// address. It may hold a token, so it’s kept secret and only its host is shown.
fields.urlKeepHint: Leave it empty to keep the saved address, which is never shown again.
fields.formatJsonHint: Signed as Standard Webhooks describes, with every detail, for a system of yours.
fields.formatChatHint: A short message that Slack, Google Chat, Mattermost and Discord show as it is, in the default language.
fields.allTypesHint: Every type, also the ones added later.
fields.staffOnly: Every webhook gets the internal requests, and the webhooks that choose them get internal notes and priorities. All three are only for the staff: send them only to a place that the staff alone read.

add.title: Add a webhook
add.description: From now on, what you choose here is sent to this address.

secret.title: Copy the signing secret
secret.description: It won’t be shown again. The receiver checks each delivery’s signature with it.
secret.label: Signing secret

webhooks.confirmFirst: Confirm it’s you with your second step before adding or changing a webhook.

page.title: Webhook
page.offNote: {reason, select, failing {It was turned off automatically because every delivery failed for 3 days. Once its receiver works, turn it on again.} gone {It was turned off automatically because its receiver answered that it’s gone for good (410 Gone).} unreadable {It was turned off automatically because its address or secret can’t be read any more. edit.title: Edit {name}
edit.description: Changes apply to what happens from now on.

test.delivered: Test delivered: the receiver answered {status, number}.

renew.title: Renew the signing secret?
renew.description: The old secret stops working at once. Deliveries the receiver refuses meanwhile are tried again, so give it the new secret soon.

remove.title: Remove {name}?
remove.description: Nothing more is sent to it, and its deliveries are deleted. This can’t be undone.

deliveries.title: Deliveries
deliveries.description: What was sent in the last 30 days and how it went, never what was sent or what the receiver answered.
deliveries.caption: Deliveries
deliveries.emptyDescription: Deliveries appear here once something it sends happens, or you send a test.
deliveries.resent: It’s sent again at the next tick.

outcome.refused_address: Its address is inside this server’s own network.

outcome.unreadable: Its address or secret can’t be read any more.

source.logo: Made from the logo, which is about square.

icon.chosen: The chosen icon, not uploaded yet.
icon.fieldDescription: A PNG or JPEG of at most {maximum, number} MB, about square and at least {minimum, number} pixels wide and high.
icon.removeDescription: The browser tab shows the icon made from the logo again, or Adiutor’s without a logo.

theme.title: Light and dark mode
theme.description: Whether each person chooses light or dark mode, or every page shows one of them. Emails are always light.

both.label: Light and dark mode
both.description: Each person chooses in the account menu or with the corner button; until then, pages follow their device.

light.label: Light mode only
light.description: Every page is light, whatever the device prefers, and there’s nothing to choose.

dark.label: Dark mode only
dark.description: Every page is dark, whatever the device prefers, and there’s nothing to choose.

colours.title: Brand colours
colours.description: The colours every page and email shows, to users and staff alike. Text always stays readable: a colour too light or too dark for that is adjusted, and the preview shows what will be used.

accent.label: Accent
accent.description: Buttons, links and focus rings, in dark mode too unless it has an accent of its own.
accent.descriptionDarkOnly: The emails and the browser tab icon, which stay light.

accentDark.label: Accent in dark mode
accentDark.description: Follows the accent until you choose a different one for dark mode. Empty it to follow the accent again.
accentDark.pick: Pick the accent for dark mode

tint.label: Tint
tint.description: The hue every grey takes, dark mode’s backgrounds too; a grey gives plain greys.
tint.descriptionLightOnly: The hue every grey takes; a grey gives plain greys.

preview.text: Secondary text, like a date or a description.

attachments.description: The files people attach to requests, replies and internal notes.

storage.description: Attached files are kept here, and each one is served from this server to whoever may read it.
storage.none: No storage is chosen yet, so nobody can attach files.

driverHints.sftp: Any server you reach over SSH, such as a storage box or a NAS.

storage.regionHint: auto on Cloudflare R2. Leave it empty for us-east-1.

storage.forcePathStyleHint: Most servers of your own, such as Garage or SeaweedFS, need this.
storage.privateKeyHint: The key's PEM text. Give a password or a private key.

sftpSecretSaved.key: A private key is saved. Leave both empty to keep it while the server, port and user stay the same.

storage.hostKeyHint: As ssh-keygen -lf prints it, starting with SHA256:. Check it on the server itself: no other key is accepted.
storage.sftpDirHint: An absolute path on the server. It must exist.
storage.saved: Storage saved. A test file was written, read back and deleted there.
storage.confirmFirst: Choosing where files are kept needs you to confirm it’s you first.

storage.notSetUpSettings: This folder isn’t set up for attached files, so files can’t be kept, read or removed there. If it’s the right folder (on a server, with its volume mounted), test and save it again to set it up.
storage.setUpDescription: Do this only if it’s the right folder: on a server, the volume that keeps the attached files must be mounted there. Files are then kept here.
storage.setUpDone: Folder set up. A test file was written, read back and deleted there.

server.title: Mail server
server.description: Sign-in links, password resets, invitations, security notices and the emails about requests are sent through this server.

server.unreadable: The server's environment chooses the mail server, but its address can't be read.
server.hostHint: The mail server's host name, e.g. smtp.yourdomain.com.

securityHints.starttls: Encrypted once connected, usually on port 587.
securityHints.none: Not encrypted. In production, only for a mail server on this computer.

server.passwordSaved: A password is saved. Leave this empty to keep it while the server, port and username stay the same.
server.fromNameHint: Shown with the address in mail apps, e.g. Adiutor.
server.fromAddressHint: An address on a domain you control, which this server may send from.
server.whoIsTold: Saving sends a test email to you through this server, then tells every staff Admin, you included.
server.saved: Mail server saved. A test email reached you through it.
server.confirmFirst: Changing the mail server needs you to confirm it’s you first.
